segments.text: This is the debrief for The Messy Export, where one function, prepare enrollment, turns a raw CSV export into an analysis-ready data frame. First, read every column as text, so nothing is guessed for you. Second, repair dates, sites, and arms with explicit rules. Third, return one clean row per participant, in a stable order.

segments.text: Line two reads every column as character, trims whitespace, and treats both empty strings and the text N, A, as missing values. Then unique drops the exact duplicate rows the export contains. Dates arrive in three formats, so parse them in passes. Try year, month, day first, then fill only the values still missing, first with the American format, and finally with day, month name, year.
segments.caption: Line 2 reads every column as character, trims whitespace, and treats empty strings and "NA" as missing. Then unique() drops the exact duplicate rows the export contains. Dates arrive in three formats, so parse them in passes. Try %Y-%m-%d first, then fill only the values still missing, first with %m/%d/%Y, and finally with %d %b %Y.

visual.title: Read as text, parse in passes

segments.text: Now build the output with an explicit type for every column. Site codes are trimmed, upper-cased, and given their hyphen by one regular expression. The arm column is cleaned and turned into a factor with fixed levels, placebo, then treatment. Finally, sort by participant I D, so the same input always gives the same row order.

The arm column is cleaned and turned into a factor with fixed levels: Placebo, then Treatment. Finally, sort by participant_id, so the same input always gives the same row order.

segments.text: Three mistakes account for most failed attempts. Parsing every date with one format turns the other two formats into missing values, and the dates check fails. Leaving empty strings as empty text, instead of missing, fails the values check. And anything hard-coded, like particular I Ds or a row count, passes on the sample but fails on a second export it has never seen.
segments.caption: Three mistakes account for most failed attempts. Parsing every date with one format turns the other two formats into NA, and the dates check fails. Leaving empty strings as "" instead of NA fails the values check. And anything hard-coded, like particular IDs or a row count, passes on the sample but fails on a second export it has never seen.
